result.keywords: This paper examines how longitudinal learning traces can be transformed into reflective dashboards that support both individual and group sensemaking. Building on work in temporality, team analysis, and learning visualization, it synthesizes techniques for segmenting activity over time, comparing temporal patterns across participants, and presenting context-sensitive summaries to learners and educators. The article argues that careful attention to how data are collected, interpreted, and displayed is essential when analytics are intended to guide collaboration, self-regulation, and intervention design. It concludes with a research agenda for evaluating dashboard fidelity, temporal granularity, and ethical considerations in multi-user learning environments
result.title: Designing Reflective Dashboards for Longitudinal Collaboration Analytics.
